children: Iron ore futures were little changed on Tuesday, as traders weighed expectations of a pickup in port arrivals following elevated global shipments against a private survey showing accelerating factory activity in China.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
traded steady at 725 yuan ($107.88) a metric ton, as of 0315 GMT.
The benchmark September iron ore (SZZFU6) on the Singapore Exchange was flat at $99.6 a ton.
Global iron ore shipments rose 2.73 million tons week-on-week to 35.72 million tons from August 24-30, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
Iron ore arrivals at 47 Chinese ports fell 7.66 million tons week-on-week to 19.52 million tons over the same period, Mysteel data showed.

A notable pullback in domestic port arrivals has caused a phased contraction in short-term supply, providing some bottom support for prices, analysts from Chinese broker Everbright Futures said in a note. The analysts added that the high level of global shipments points to a gradual resumption in port arrivals, limiting gains.

Global iron ore production growth is expected to accelerate to an average of 2.2% a year over 2026-2030, up from 1.2% over the prior five years, lifting annual output to 3,037 million tons by 2030, according to a report by analysts at research firm BMI.
China's manufacturing sector expanded at a faster pace in August as output, new orders and exports all accelerated, a private-sector survey showed on Tuesday.

The RatingDog China General Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, rose to 51.5 in August from 50.9 in July, staying above the 50-mark that separates growth from contraction.
